changes: REVISION AFTER THE TEST, 1: THE ENDING IS NOW SEEN, AND IT IS A MATCHDAY TRUTH. Outsider: 'make the last joke something I see, not something I'm told'. Fan: give me 'the moment at the gate where that case obviously is not getting in'. Three viewers asked why the suitcase goes to the stadium at all. The film now ends at the gate: Big Yellow is parked across a turnstile gate half its width, Timo hugs it and says he loves it, Luna points her thumb at the gate and says 'It can't come in, Timo.', and his eyes snap open at the camera. The viewers' own question is now the punchline. The look into the camera, which two viewers named second best, is kept. 'This is the small one' is not lost: it moved to Luna's first answer, where the picture shows the joke at once (she pats a suitcase as big as a washing machine while she says it).

REVISION 2: THE BAG HUT IS OUT OF THE PILOT. Two viewers wondered if they had missed a joke and the other two never saw it. The gate now answers the question. The hut stays in the bible for a later film where it is the story.

REVISION 3: 'ONE NIGHT' IS SAID ONCE, NOT THREE TIMES. Fan, outsider and native all felt told the joke before they had looked at the picture. The top line keeps 'one night'. Timo's line becomes a roast, 'Did you bring your whole house?', and Luna's echo 'Yes! One night!' is cut. If the top line is ever removed, Timo's line goes back to 'It's one night!' (recorded in the same session).

REVISION 4: THE TOP LINE STAYS LONGER AND LOOKS LIKE THE APP. The muted viewer read half of it in 1.8 seconds and said this kind of line normally stays up; the native viewer said the words are fine and the violet brand plate is the tell. It now stays for the whole first shot (0 to 5.0 seconds) in plain white letters with a thin dark outline. Nothing is spoken for the first two seconds, so it can be read alone.

REVISION 5: CAPTIONS LOSE THE BRAND LOOK. Muted viewer: 'very tidy captions in brand colours with full stops' give away an advert. All captions are now plain white with a thin dark outline, no violet plate, no full stop at the end. Still only the spoken line, still one size and one place.

REVISION 6: WHERE THEY ARE GOING IS CLEAR IN FRAME ONE. Muted viewer and outsider did not know what Timo points at ('four tall poles'). The rim of the stadium with flags and four lit floodlights now shows over the hill, in clear sky at his fingertip and below the line of text, and two still fan shapes on the street face uphill. This gives up a little of the surprise at the hilltop; the long straight street down is still new there.

REVISION 7: THE MUSIC. The three viewers who heard the film named the same second as the moment it became an advert: the group 'oh-oh-oh' with the clap pattern on the ride, which came back on the logo card. Both are cut from the film and from the card. Two said the log drum is not new any more: a rubbery organ bass replaces it. The native heard the tick-tock as a cartoon trick or a wink at the app's name: the clock tick is gone, the music no longer plays each character, and the working title changes from 'Tick Tock Clap' to 'Downhill'. What stays is what all four named as the best moment: the 'No', the dead air, the drop on the cut.

REVISION 8: MORE BITE, LESS TIDY. Native, muted and fan: real friends roast each other; the lines sound written; saying the name first every time is how a kids' show talks. Now: a roast and a proud comeback in shot 1; Timo's scream on the ride is her name ('LUNAAA!'); 'Too slow!' shouted at the cat replaces 'Byeee!' (two viewers called that kids' show); Luna's last line gets him. The name-first formula and the yes-echo are cut. Each name is heard once, where a real person would say it. This also answers the outsider's 'Timo is mostly reactions': he roasts, he gets cocky, and then the gate gets him.

REVISION 9: YOU SEE WHO TALKS AT THE END. Muted viewer could not tell who spoke in the last close-up because Luna's mouth was behind her arm. Her whole face is now in view when she says the last line.

REVISION 10: IT IS THE SAME CAT. The native wondered for a second if the cat at the bottom was a different one, because it sat waiting before they got there. In shot 6 it is now still on the same walk, on the same kind of wall, in the same screen direction, tail up; the friends overtake it exactly as it overtook them. In shot 2 it looks back without stopping and keeps walking.

REVISION 11: THE CARD. All four did not know what Venuvoy is; fan and native read the friends' scarf as the company's scarf once it lay on the card. The scarf is off the card (it belongs to the two friends). The small label changes from 'football trips' to 'football trip app', one word more, because the question was 'an app or a travel company?'. The clap sting is gone; Luna's laugh and the crowd run under the card. The fuller answer and how to say the name go in the account line, not in the film. The card stays two seconds: it is the brand's only signature. This label needs the client's yes; the alternative is the name alone.

REVISION 12: LESS PRESCHOOL, MORE MATCHDAY. Outsider: the toy town 'with bunting' looks like a preschool series and nothing is messy. Fan: nothing is specific to football. The bunting is replaced by plain home-colour scarves tied to balconies and a lamp post; the floodlights are already on; drums are heard from the ground; Big Yellow is scuffed; after the ride there is dust on the suitcase and on Timo's knees and both scarves are blown back.

REVISION 13: THE INTERACTION LIST IS REBUILT FROM WHAT VIEWERS POINTED AT. Kept: the eyes that follow the cat together, his V above her V, the pats, the 'Trust me / No' pair, the look at us. Added because viewers named them: the shoulder clamp, her twisting round to check his face, the roast and comeback, the name scream. Cut: the five-clap handshake (it was the jingle), the name with a full stop, the yes-echo.

NOT CHANGED ON PURPOSE AFTER THE TEST. (a) No race against kick-off, although the fan asked for it: in the earlier test a deadline line produced four different guesses; urgency is only the lit floodlights and the drums. (b) What is inside the suitcase stays closed, although the outsider asked: Timo's roast now raises the question in the film, and it is the standing question of the series. (c) The art-toy look, the cat and the 'No' cut stay: the client chose the look, and the cut is the best moment for all four.

HONEST LIMIT. All four viewers said the film reads as a well-made brand film, not as something a person posted. This revision removes the tells they named (the jingle, the brand plate, the tidy lines, the scarf on the card). It does not pretend to be a person's post: the designed look and the two-second card stay, and the film carries the AI label.

BIBLE LINES THAT NEED A YES. Rule 9 (no header, never two texts at once): one top line, and two texts at once in shot 1 only. Caption style: plain white instead of cream on violet. Four lines per film: six captioned lines, the same number that scored 9 for understanding. Music theme: no chant, no five-clap, no tick-tock, new working title. End card: no scarf, new label, no claps. World: scarves on balconies instead of bunting. The silent gate with all text covered stays as the safeguard.

KEPT FROM VERSION 3, client's words 'interactions between the characters': back-and-forth in shots 1, 3 and 7 (two people, one short line each); the shared look in shot 2; her check and his V in shot 5; the head pats in shot 7.

KEPT FROM VERSION 3, formats and sound research: 'Trust me.' before the 'No'; the 'No' in a fixed rhythm; a third of a second of air; the drop exactly on the hard cut; shot 4 at 2.0 seconds and shot 5 at 3.0 so the turn starts on a downbeat; his scream turning into 'Yes!' so the film reads as No, then Yes; plain hard cuts with no effects.

KEPT FROM VERSION 3, series and formats research: sound from frame one with no intro; the card at two seconds with Luna's laugh under it; the cut from the card straight back to the bump of frame one, so the film loops.

CLIENT'S WORDS 'the trends of right now', said plainly: the story of the pilot is not a trend. The research found no current trend for an overpacking friend or a suitcase ride. What is current is the way it is told: the one line in the app's own look, the cut on the beat with silence before the drop, a club beat instead of a jingle, the post text, and the list of formats below.

pilot.title: One Night
pilot.hook_text: When your friend packs for one night. DECISION: yes, one line, changed in two ways after the test. (1) IT STAYS LONGER: from frame one to the cut at the end of shot 1 (0 to 5.0 seconds) instead of 1.8 seconds. The muted viewer read only half of it and said this kind of line normally stays up. Nothing is spoken for the first two seconds, so the line is read alone; after that it does not change, and the spoken captions appear lower down. Two texts at once for three seconds, in shot 1 only, is normal on the platform and is a deliberate exception to bible rule 9. (2) IT LOOKS LIKE THE APP, NOT LIKE THE BRAND: plain white bold letters with a thin dark outline, two centred lines near the top, below the platform's top bar, sentence case, no full stop, no emoji, no violet plate. The native viewer said the words are fine and the branded plate is the tell. It is baked into the master so the same file goes to all three platforms. WHY IT STAYS: the muted viewer said it is what tells him the film is for his age and not a kids' cartoon; the outsider said it told them at once what they were watching; it is the first recommendation of the formats research. NOT NEEDED FOR THE STORY: the giant suitcase, the tiny backpack and Timo's face tell it, and the silent gate is run with every text covered. It is now the only place where 'one night' is said, so the spoken lines add a joke instead of repeating it. If it is ever taken off, Timo's line goes back to 'It's one night!' and nothing else changes.
pilot.retell: His friend brought a giant suitcase for one night, and pushing it up the hill was so slow that a cat overtook them, so they rode it down the other side to the stadium, shot past the cat, and he ended up hugging the suitcase at the gate, where it was too big to go in.

shots.place: A small square outside the train station of the invented football town: a plain cream arch with a soft cream-and-teal train carriage standing behind it. Late afternoon, low golden sun from the left, worn cobbles. No bunting: a few plain cream-and-violet scarves are tied to a lamp post and a balcony rail, as on a match day. Behind Timo a street climbs steeply. Over its top, in clear sky, the upper rim of the stadium shows: a cream curve with plain flags and four floodlight masts that are already switched on. Two still, soft shapes of fans with scarves stand on the street, facing uphill.
shots.seen: From the first frame a scuffed yellow suitcase as big as a washing machine stands in the middle of the picture. On the left stands Luna, short, in a coral football shirt, one hand flat on its lid, chin up, grinning proudly. On the right, close to the camera, stands Timo, tall, in a teal jacket, one thumb under the strap of a tiny backpack, his other arm stretched out and pointing up the steep street at the lit floodlights and the rim of the stadium over the hill. Both wear the same teal-and-coral scarf. Timo's eyes travel from the bottom of the suitcase up to its top. He turns his face to Luna and speaks with a flat face, and his pointing arm sinks while he speaks. Luna pats the lid twice and answers, even prouder.
shots.heard: Timo, flat, at 2.0 s: 'Did you bring your whole house?' Luna, proud, at 3.6 s: 'This is the small one!' Natural sound: a last rattle of small wheels and one heavy bump on the first beat, the hum of the train, a crowd and drums far away over the hill, two hollow pats on the lid at 4.0 and 4.5. Music: the groove starts on frame one with no intro, shaker and rim click only, kept low under the lines; the bass riff enters at 4.0 on her first pat.
shots.caption: Did you bring your whole house? (2.0 to 3.5) then This is the small one! (3.6 to 5.0). The hook line stays at the top from 0 to 5.0 and goes on the cut.
shots.start_picture: Everything is already in place. Big Yellow is parked dead centre, satin yellow with scuffs and scratches, its wheels just inside the bottom edge. Luna on the left, facing us, one hand flat on the lid, chin up, a proud closed-mouth grin, eyes on Timo. Timo on the right, nearest the camera, three-quarters to us, his face already turned to the suitcase with his eyes on its bottom edge, mouth closed, eyebrows tilted up in the middle; the arm without the watch is stretched out and points up the street; the thumb of the watch arm is under the backpack strap. At his fingertip, about one third of the way down the frame, in clear sky: the cream rim of the stadium with flags and four lit masts over the hilltop. The top fifth of the frame is plain sky for the line of text, and no face sits in the caption band. The clip adds only: his eyes climb and he speaks as the arm sinks; she pats twice and speaks. Nothing rolls; the bump is sound. Plan B: her answer as a second, closer clip of the same idea (Luna and the lid only).

shots.place: A steep cobbled street between painted houses, seen from the side: it climbs from right to left. Same golden sun. A garden wall runs along the far side, its top higher than everyone's heads. Plain home-colour scarves hang from one balcony. Over the top of the street, the rim of the stadium and its four lit masts, bigger now.
shots.who: Luna, Timo and the ginger cat
shots.seen: The yellow suitcase is stuck halfway up the steep street and hardly moves. We see the friends from the knees up. On the left, above the suitcase, Luna leans back as in a tug-of-war, both hands on its handle, cheeks puffed out. On the right, below it, Timo pushes with both hands and one shoulder, his cheek squashed flat against the yellow shell, his face towards us. On top of the wall behind them a fat ginger cat strolls up the hill with its tail up. It passes Timo, passes the suitcase, passes Luna. Both friends' eyes follow the cat together; their heads do not move. Without stopping, the cat looks back at them once and keeps walking. The friends' eyes leave the cat and find each other.
shots.heard: No words. Natural sound: small wheels grinding slowly on cobbles, both friends puffing, trainers slipping, one small 'mrrp' from the cat in a gap. Music: the round bass riff and the shaker carry the shot at a lazy level; nothing in the music imitates the action; at 8.0 it thins to bass and shaker.
shots.caption: none
shots.start_picture: Side view, street climbing from right to left, friends from the knees up so that feet and wheels are out of frame. Both are in held strain poses: Luna on the left, facing the suitcase, leaning back with both hands on the front handle, cheeks puffed; Timo on the right with both hands and one shoulder on the shell and his cheek already flat on it, face to the camera. The wall is on the far side with its top above all heads; the cat is on it above Timo, in mid-step, tail up like a question mark, with clear empty wall ahead of it. The clip adds only: the cat walks along the wall and turns its head back once; the two pairs of eyes follow it and then meet. The friends move a hand's width at most. Plan B: the cat is generated alone on the wall and laid over the friends' clip in the edit.

shots.place: The top of the hill, same golden sun. On the far side the street falls away, long and straight, with roofs stepping down, to the stadium below: a round cream bowl with four lit floodlight masts and flags, bright in the sun, with small still shapes of fans around it.
shots.seen: The stadium lies below them at the bottom of a long straight street; we see it in the gap between the two friends. On the left the suitcase stands on the last flat stones before the slope, and Luna is already sitting on the front half of its lid, turned towards Timo, feet off the ground, with a huge grin. One of her arms points straight down the hill at the stadium. She says two words to him. On the right Timo stands with both palms up and says no. Luna pats the empty half of the lid behind her, twice. Timo shakes his head, says no three more times and takes one step back.
shots.heard: Luna, at 8.6 s: 'Trust me.' Timo, at 10.0 s: 'No.' Two hollow pats on the lid (10.5 and 11.0). Timo, 11.5 to 12.0: 'No, no, no.' Then about a third of a second of nothing: outdoor air and one squeak of a wheel. Luna grins without a sound, so nothing covers the last 'no'. Natural sound: a far crowd and drums rising from below. Music: bass and shaker under 'Trust me'; the shaker alone from the first 'No'; everything stops dead at 12.0. This shot is unchanged from the tested version: all four viewers named it the best moment.
shots.caption: Trust me (8.6 to 10.0) then No. No, no, no (10.0 to 12.5)
shots.start_picture: Camera on the hilltop at Luna's seated eye level, three-quarter view, so that the empty back half of the lid is in plain sight. The drop is painted clearly: roofs stepping down, the stadium below eye level in the gap between the friends. The suitcase stands on the last flat stones. Luna already sits sideways on the front half, feet off the ground, one arm already pointing down at the stadium (held, it does not move), her other hand flat on the empty half of the lid, a huge closed-mouth grin, eyes on Timo. Timo stands on the right in profile with both palms already up at chest height, eyebrows tilted, mouth closed. The clip adds only: she speaks and pats twice; he speaks, shakes his head and takes one step back.

shots.place: The long downhill street, sun flashing between the houses; the walls on both sides are soft bands of colour.
shots.who: Luna and Timo, both sitting on the suitcase
shots.seen: Hard cut. Both are riding the suitcase down the hill, straight towards the camera, which flies backwards just ahead of them. We see them from the chest up; the yellow lid is a wide bar across the bottom of the picture. Luna sits in front with both arms up in a wide V and her mouth wide open in a laugh. Timo sits behind her, his face in the gap above her head: eyes huge, mouth wide open in a scream, both hands clamped on her shoulders. Scarves and shirts flap. The street behind them streaks past.
shots.heard: Timo, as one long scream that starts on the first frame: 'LUNAAA!' Luna whoops. Natural sound: wheels roaring on cobbles, wind. Music: the full groove (kick, congas, organ bass, organ stabs) lands exactly on the cut, with his scream in place of a crash. No chant and no claps.
shots.caption: none (the scream is her name; its picture is his face)
shots.start_picture: Both are already seated in mid-ride, seen from the chest up, the yellow lid a wide bar across the bottom. Luna in front, both arms already up in a wide V, mouth wide open in a laugh. Timo behind her, his face in the gap above her head, eyes huge, mouth already wide open, both hands already clamped on her shoulders. Scarves stream back; the background is soft bands of colour. The clip adds only: cloth flapping, the background streaking, a small bounce of the two bodies. Hair stays one solid shape.

shots.place: The same downhill street, further down, same sun.
shots.who: Luna and Timo, both sitting on the suitcase
shots.seen: The same picture one cut later, a little wider, so that all four hands are inside the frame. Timo is now laughing as hard as Luna, his eyes squeezed into happy lines, and both his arms are up in the same wide V as hers, his V above her V. Luna has twisted round to look up at him over her shoulder, checking his face, laughing; he looks down at her. Both pump their raised arms twice. The street streaks past behind them.
shots.heard: Timo: the scream turns into a shouted 'Yes!' and a big laugh. Luna laughs over him. Natural sound: wheels roaring, wind. Music: the same groove runs on; one short vocal chop answers on the downbeat at 14.5, where his 'Yes!' lands. No group voices and no clap pattern: their two voices are the hook.
shots.caption: none (the 'Yes!' is a shout inside a laugh; its picture is the two V's)
shots.start_picture: The same seat, a little wider, all four hands inside the frame. Timo's arms are already up in the same wide V as Luna's, above hers; his eyes are already squeezed into happy lines and his mouth is open in a laugh. Luna is already twisted half round, looking up at him over her shoulder, laughing. The clip adds only: both pump their arms twice and their eyes hold each other. Plan B if the twist fails: Luna faces forward and only Timo's V is new.

shots.place: Near the bottom of the same street: the top of a garden wall of the same kind as on the way up, in golden sun, soft painted houses behind it.
shots.who: The ginger cat; Luna and Timo only as a streak
shots.seen: The same ginger cat, still on its walk: it strolls along the top of a wall from right to left, exactly as it did on the way up, tail up, eyes half closed. Below it the yellow suitcase with the two friends on it, all four arms up, shoots past in the same direction and overtakes it: a streak of yellow, coral and teal. The wind flattens the cat's ears and blows its fur and whiskers forward. It stops dead with one front paw in the air. Its eyes are huge.
shots.heard: Timo, laughing, rushing past: 'Too slow!' Natural sound: a fast rattle of wheels, a gust of wind, then one small surprised 'mrrow' in the quiet. Music: drums and bass drop out for this one shot; only the shaker stays.
shots.caption: none (a shout from a streak; the picture is the two of them overtaking the cat)
shots.start_picture: The cat in mid-step on top of the wall, a little right of centre, walking left, tail up like a question mark, eyes half closed, with clear empty wall ahead of it. Below the wall an empty strip of sunny street, where the streak is laid in during the edit. Still camera. The clip adds only: two calm steps, then ears, fur and whiskers blow to the left and the cat freezes with one paw lifted and round eyes. No head turn is needed, because the friends leave in the direction it already faces.

shots.place: In front of the stadium gate, low golden sun from the left. The gate is a narrow cream doorway between two round posts with a waist-high violet bar across it, one person wide. Above and through it: the bright warm glow of the ground, plain flags, and a few still, soft shapes of fans holding cream-and-violet scarves up. There is no hut in this picture.
shots.seen: Two clips of one idea. First, framed like the first shot: Luna on the left, the yellow suitcase in the middle, Timo on the right. The suitcase stands right across the gate and is twice as wide as the gap between the posts; its lid is higher than the violet bar. A last puff of dust drifts away from its wheels; there is dust on its lower half and on Timo's knees, and both scarves have blown back over their shoulders. Timo is on his knees with his chest against the suitcase and both arms spread wide along its lid. He looks up, beaming, and speaks. Then he lays his cheek on the lid and closes his eyes, smiling. Luna leans on the lid on one elbow and grins down at him, slowly shaking her head. Second, closer: Timo's cheek on the yellow lid, eyes shut, smiling. Luna is above him with her whole face in clear view, one hand resting on his flat-top, the thumb of her other hand pointing back at the narrow gate, which sits in the gap between their heads. She says five words, grinning, and pats his head twice as she says them. Timo's eyes snap open and look straight into the camera. His arms tighten round the suitcase. Luna bursts out laughing.
shots.heard: Timo, at 20.7 s: 'I love this suitcase.' A happy sigh. Luna, grinning, at 23.8 s: 'It can't come in, Timo.' Two soft pats on his head (24.0 and 24.5). At 25.0 everything stops: one second of the roar of the ground and nothing else, on his open eyes. Then Luna's big laugh from about 25.6, not cut clean, running on under the card. Music: the groove returns on the downbeat at 20.5, lower, with one warm round organ note; it thins to the bass under Luna's line and stops dead at 25.0.
shots.caption: I love this suitcase (20.7 to 22.4) then, alone, after it has gone: It can't come in, Timo (23.8 to 25.6)
shots.start_picture: TWO start pictures. (a) Wide, composed like shot 1: the suitcase side-on in the middle, parked right against the narrow gate, whose two posts and violet bar show above the lid in the centre with the glow behind them. Timo already on his knees on the right, chest against the suitcase, arms spread along the lid, face lifted, beaming, mouth closed. Luna on the left, already leaning on the lid on one elbow, closed-mouth grin, eyes on him. Dust on the wheels and on his knees, scarves blown back. The clip adds only: he speaks, lowers his cheek and shuts his eyes; she shakes her head. (b) Closer, over the lid: his cheek already on the lid, eyes shut, smiling; Luna's face above his in full view, mouth closed in a grin, one hand already flat on his flat-top, her other thumb already pointing back over her shoulder at the gate; the gate posts and bar in the gap between their heads; both faces above the caption band. The clip adds only: she speaks while her hand pats twice; his eyes snap open to the lens. Nobody's arm goes round the other.

pilot.end_card: Two seconds (26.5 to 28.5) on the plain warm cream card: the word VENUVOY in deep violet in the middle and three small words below it: 'football trip app'. The scarf is no longer on the card: it belongs to the two friends, not to the company. Sound: Luna's laugh and the roar of the ground run on; the groove comes back for exactly one bar and stops on one dry rim hit at 28.0. No clap sting, no chant, no logo animation, no link, no slogan. The card cuts straight back to frame one, where the bump of the suitcase is beat one again, so the film loops. Shots 26.5 seconds plus card 2.0: 28.5 seconds.

interactions: 'TRUST ME.' / 'NO. NO, NO, NO.' (the offer and the refusal; the sound the series owns). The one who offers says 'Trust me.' with a big gesture; the other holds both palms up, shakes the head and takes one step back. Always the same rhythm: 'No.' on one, two pats on two and three, 'no, no, no' on four, a third of a second of air, hard cut. Whichever friend says which half. All four test viewers named this the best moment, so nothing about it changes. Drawn in 3 seconds: the palms are already up in the start picture.

THE NAME SCREAM. On the first frame after the cut, the one who said 'No' screams the other one's name ('LUNAAA!', in another film 'TIMOOO!'), and inside three seconds the scream turns into a laugh and a 'Yes!'. It is how friends blame each other, and it gives a cold viewer the name without a label. Drawn in 3 seconds: the mouth is already wide open in the start picture.

THE PAT-PAT (the teasing touch). Two flat-hand pats in the beat. Luna pats what she is offering: her suitcase ('this one'), the empty seat ('sit here'). And whoever was right pats the other one's head twice: Luna only when Timo is down at her height, Timo from above without looking. Pats, never a hug: friends like brother and sister. Drawn in 3 seconds: the hand is already flat on the surface and only lifts and lands twice.

THE DOUBLE V (the picture after every 'No' cut). Luna in front, Timo behind and above her, both with both arms up in the same wide V. A short V inside a tall V reads at thumbnail size and with the sound off, and it says that the one who refused has joined in. The muted viewer named it. Drawn in 3 seconds: the arms are already up and only pump twice. It can be done standing anywhere, so two friends can copy it.

FOUR EYES. Both pairs of eyes follow the same thing together with the heads perfectly still (the cat, a tray of food, a falling streamer), then the eyes leave it and find each other. No words. All four viewers named it as the moment the two felt like real friends. Drawn in 3 seconds, and the safest shared move for generated video, because only eyes move.

THE CLAMP. When one of them is scared, both hands clamp on the other one's shoulders from behind, and the other one does not even notice. In the pilot it is Timo on the ride; in a later film it is Luna behind Timo. Drawn in 3 seconds: the hands are already on the shoulders and only the fingers squeeze.

THE CHECK. In the middle of the chaos the one who started it twists round to look at the other one's face. When their eyes meet, the scream becomes a shared laugh. Two viewers pointed at exactly this in the ride. Drawn in 3 seconds: the head is already turned; only the eyes meet and the laugh grows.

THE ROAST AND THE COMEBACK (how they talk). One flat roast, one proud comeback, then they move on. 'Did you bring your whole house?' / 'This is the small one!' Later: 'Did you sleep in that shirt?' / 'Twice!' and 'You made a list for breakfast?' / 'Two lists.' Three rules keep it warm: the roast is about the thing and never about the person; the comeback never defends, it doubles down; and the one who was roasted is proved right by the end of the film. Drawn in 3 seconds: one flat face, one grin.

THE LOOK AT US. Once per film and never more, the one who has just been proved wrong looks straight into the camera for a second, in silence, as if at the third friend who is filming. In the pilot it is Timo's eyes snapping open at the gate. Drawn in 3 seconds: closed eyes, open eyes.

THE LIFT (the handshake; from the second film, not in the pilot). A fist bump across the height gap. Timo holds his fist out at his own chest height, which is above Luna's head, and looks away; she is on tiptoe and cannot reach; then his fist comes straight down like a lift and bumps hers. Fists, never hugs. Drawn in 3 seconds: his fist high, hers stretched up below it, one move down. It has not been tested: if a viewer calls it staged, it goes.

music.direction: CHANGED AFTER THE TEST: A CLUB BEAT UNDER TWO FRIENDS, NOT A THEME SONG. Drums and bass only, bright, with a bounce, and one tiny pitched vocal chop. It starts on the groove in the first half second, stops dead before the drop and ends dry. The hook of the series is no longer sung. It is their two voices: 'Trust me.' / 'No. No, no, no.', a third of a second of air, the drop, 'LUNAAA!' turning into a laugh. WHAT WAS CUT AND WHY: the three viewers who heard the film named the same second as the moment it became an advert: the group 'oh-oh-oh' with the clap pattern on the ride, which then came back on the logo card ('exactly what a brand jingle sounds like'). The chant and the five-clap are out of the film and out of the card. Two viewers said the log drum is not new any more, so a rubbery organ bass takes its place. One heard the tick-tock as a cartoon trick or a wink at the app's name, so the clock tick is gone, the music no longer plays each character, and the working title changes from 'Tick Tock Clap' to 'Downhill'. WHAT STAYS: all four viewers named the 'No', the silence and the drop as the best moment, and the outsider said the pats landing on the beat feel like TikTok. The edit still cuts to the beat, and the bump, the pats and the scream stay on it. WHY THIS READS AS CURRENT: the sound research describes this autumn's feed as club music led by drums and bassline, bright, 120 to 135 beats a minute, with tiny chopped vocal hooks (afro house reported as the sound of 2026, UK garage as the wave of the summer), and says comedy sketches run on their own audio with a light bed, not on a song. The same research lists the signs of advert music: a group chant with claps, whistling, bright piano, a riser, a fade. HONEST LIMITS: the native viewer said a sound he does not know is no trend he is let in on. No prompt fixes that, and the fix he means is not legal for a brand. The sentence for the founder: 'Trendy means it sounds like this month's feed; it cannot be this month's hit, because labels are suing brands for exactly that, and a sound we own is the one that can become ours.' The genre evidence comes from search summaries of trackers and reports, not from the app itself. HOW TO CHOOSE: generate brief A and brief B, 64 seconds each, four variations, vocals allowed, never an artist or song name in the prompt. Play each under the pilot on a phone speaker at half volume to three people aged 18 to 25 and ask one question: 'advert, or somebody's video?'. Take the one that gets 'somebody's video' most often. Brief C is the loud option and the riskiest: it sounds like one country and can turn aggressive. Then lock ONE master for the whole series, split it into stems and never generate the music again for a later film. Run the master through a song-recognition app before use. MIX: natural sound as loud as the music; music 6 to 9 dB lower under spoken lines; start at about -14 LUFS with peaks under -1 dBTP and judge in mono on a phone.

briefs.name: A. Downhill (afro house with an organ bass, 120 beats a minute). Recommended: the pilot is timed on it.
briefs.style_prompt: Sunny afro house club track, drums and bass only. Exactly 120 BPM, 4/4, F major. No intro, no fade: starts on beat one with a tight dry shaker and a rim click. At 8 seconds a rubbery two-bar organ bassline joins, with a mid-range knock that carries on a phone speaker. At 16 seconds it thins to bass and shaker for 8 seconds, then one beat of total silence. Then the drop: soft round four-on-the-floor kick, congas, shekere, off-beat open hi-hat, short warm organ stabs pumping with the kick, and one pitched-up one-syllable vocal chop answering every second bar, no words. After 16 seconds a 6-second breakdown of shaker and bass, then the full groove returns and stops dead on one dry rim hit. Dry, close, hand-played. No lyrics, no sung melody, no choir or group chant, no handclap pattern, no log drum, no clock tick, no guitar, piano, whistling or risers.

briefs.name: B. Sunny 2-Step (UK garage bounce, 130 beats a minute). The challenger: the most 2026 for UK and European feeds, less sure elsewhere.
briefs.style_prompt: Sunny, cheeky UK garage club track with a speed-garage bounce, drums and bass first. Exactly 130 BPM, 4/4, G major. No intro, no fade: starts on beat one with shuffled closed hi-hats and a rim click. At 7 seconds a swung 2-step pattern joins (kick on one, a late skipping kick, rimshot on two and four) with a warm, bouncy two-bar organ bass riff, clear on a phone speaker. At 15 seconds it thins to bass and hats, then one beat of total silence. Then the drop: the full 2-step groove with a deeper bass, bright filtered chord stabs and chopped, pitched-up one-syllable vocal slices used as rhythm, no words. A short breakdown, then the groove returns and stops dead on one dry rimshot. Dry, punchy, swung, warm, a little crunchy. No MC, no rap, no lyrics, no choir or chant, no handclap pattern, no sirens, no air horn, no dark reese bass, no wobble, no piano chords, no risers.

briefs.name: C. Matchday Drums (street drums with a Brazilian funk bounce, 130 beats a minute). The loud option: closest to the drums of a ground, riskiest because it sounds like one country.
briefs.style_prompt: Bright daylight street-drum club track with a Brazilian funk bounce, percussion and sub bass only. Exactly 130 BPM, 4/4, major key. No intro, no fade: starts on beat one with a tamborim pattern and a shaker. At 7 seconds the tamborzao rhythm joins on real hand drums: low surdo, pandeiro, agogo bells landing a little late, a short punchy kick and a two-note bounce bass that carries on a phone speaker. At 15 seconds it thins to bass and shaker, then one beat of total silence. Then the drop: the full drum corps, louder, with staccato one-syllable shout hits used as rhythm, no words. A short breakdown, then the groove returns and stops dead on one dry drum hit. Playful, like fans drumming outside a ground in the sun. No melody, no lyrics, no choir or chant, no handclap pattern, no distorted cowbell, no drift phonk, no dark or aggressive mood, no sirens, no whistles, no risers.

music.edit_plan: GRID: 120 beats a minute, one beat is half a second. Only four points must be exact: the stop at 12.0, the drop at 12.5, the return at 20.5 and the stop at 25.0. Everything else stays loose. Never squeeze a spoken line to fit: move the music, not the mouth. SHOT 1 (0.0 to 5.0): the heavy bump of the suitcase is beat one; shaker and rim click only, with no intro, low under the two lines; Luna's two pats land on 4.0 and 4.5, and the bass riff enters on the first pat. SHOT 2 (5.0 to 8.5): bass riff and shaker at a lazy level; the grinding wheels sit in time like a second shaker; the cat's 'mrrp' sits in a gap; at 8.0 it thins to bass and shaker. SHOT 3 (8.5 to 12.5): bass and shaker under 'Trust me.' at 8.6; 'No.' on 10.0 with only the shaker left; the two lid pats on 10.5 and 11.0 are the drum fill; 'no, no, no' from 11.5; at 12.0 everything stops dead; about a third of a second of outdoor air and one wheel squeak. SHOT 4 (12.5 to 14.5): the drop lands on the first frame of the hard cut, with 'LUNAAA!' in place of a crash; the bar count restarts here. SHOT 5 (14.5 to 17.5): starts on a downbeat; 'Yes!' and one vocal chop on 14.5; the arms pump on 15.5 and 16.0; no chant and no claps. SHOT 6 (17.5 to 20.5): drums and bass drop out, shaker only; the streak and 'Too slow!' at about 18.3; the gust; the small 'mrrow' alone at about 19.5. SHOT 7 (20.5 to 26.5): the groove returns on a downbeat, lower, with one warm organ note under 'I love this suitcase.'; it thins to the bass under 'It can't come in, Timo.' at 23.8; her two pats on his head land on 24.0 and 24.5; at 25.0 everything stops dead on his open eyes: one second of the far roar only, then Luna's laugh from about 25.6. CARD (26.5 to 28.5): the groove comes back for exactly one bar under her laugh and stops on one dry rim hit at 28.0; half a second of air; the cut back to frame one puts the bump on beat one again. The second stop at 25.0 rhymes with the 'No' gap but has no drop after it, so the signature stays single. IF BRIEF B OR C WINS (130 beats a minute): do not re-time the picture. Cut the music in blocks from the stems so that its stop, drop, return and second stop land on the same four seconds; between those points the beat does not have to match every cut. A film that cuts on every bar line feels like a template.
music.platform_sound_plan: THE RULE, said plainly to the founder: a brand account cannot put this month's hit under its video on TikTok, Reels or Shorts, in any form (sped up, a cover, five seconds, credit in the caption, or posted from a personal account). Labels sued several brands for exactly this in 2025 and 2026. THE PLAN: (1) One owned master, mixed into the film file. The same file goes to all three platforms on the same day, so on each it shows as the account's own original sound. (2) Before the pilot, upload a private test from the real Venuvoy account with the real master, to see what the app asks (business accounts are reported to get a music confirmation box) and whether others can reuse the sound. (3) Keep proof of rights: the prompt, the date, the job number and the paid-plan receipt of the music generator; check that the plan allows commercial use. (4) After posting, rename the sound to something findable, for example 'No. No, no, no. (Plan, No Plan)'. Never delete a posted film; set it to private if needed, because deleting can remove its sound. Never write 'use this sound'. (5) HOW TO RIDE TRENDS LEGALLY: through the format, not through the song. The research reports that trends are becoming formats more than sounds; the list of formats below is that plan. Our own seven seconds ('No', air, drop, the name scream, the laugh) are the part other people could act out with their own footage. (6) If the founder still wants a known sound once: a separate TikTok-only repost with a track from TikTok's Commercial Music Library, chosen in the app on the day with the filter for business use. It replaces our music and breaks the cut on the beat, so it is an experiment, never the main post, and that export must never be reposted to Reels or Shorts. (7) Do not use the trick of a trending sound at very low volume under our audio: unproven, legal for a brand only with library tracks, and it gives the sound credit away. LIMITS: these rules come from trade and vendor sources, not from the platforms' own help pages, and they change. Check each help centre in the week of posting. This is not legal advice.

trend_formats.name: The 'No' cut as our own sound
trend_formats.how: The same seven seconds in every film: 'Trust me.', 'No. No, no, no.', a third of a second of air, the drop on a plain hard cut, the other one's name screamed, the scream turning into a laugh. No speed ramp, no effect. It is published as a named original sound. To be honest with the client: this is a classic comedy cut, not a trend; the trend part is the silence before the drop.
trend_formats.episode_idea: I Can't See: at the back of a crowd of fans short Luna cannot see the drummers, tall Timo offers his shoulders, she says no, and one cut later it is Timo who sits on Luna's shoulders, wobbling and screaming her name, while she stands like a rock and they both see everything.
trend_formats.shelf_life: Evergreen. The device does not date; cutting on the drop is the standard edit of the platform.

trend_formats.name: One line on the first frame, in the app's own look
trend_formats.how: One line of at most seven words in plain white app-style text, on screen for the whole first shot, never needed to follow the story. 'When your friend ...' is safe but not new (the native viewer dated it to 2021). 'POV:' only when the camera really is the third friend. Never 'Types of ...' lists or labels.
trend_formats.episode_idea: Wake Up, Luna (line: 'When your friend books the first train'): at sunrise Timo is dressed and ready, Luna pulls the blanket over her head and says no, and one cut later she walks down the sunny street with her eyes shut, wrapped in the blanket, following the warm pastry he holds in front of her nose, until on the train she is wide awake eating it and he is the one asleep.
trend_formats.shelf_life: The device is evergreen; the wording goes out of fashion. Check the wording on the platform each month.

trend_formats.name: Two friends, two types, in one frame
trend_formats.how: One side-by-side picture per film that reads at thumbnail size: his thing small and neat, her thing big and messy. It is the cover of the film. The question 'Plan or No Plan: which one are you?' lives in the post text. Never the labels 'Type A' and 'Type B', and Luna is never the flake who costs Timo something.
trend_formats.episode_idea: Try It: Timo unwraps the neat sandwiches he packed while Luna holds a huge steaming flatbread from a street stand under his nose, he says no, and one cut later he has a flatbread in each hand and sauce on his chin while Luna happily eats his sandwiches.
trend_formats.shelf_life: Evergreen, but crowded since 2025. It works only when tied to one concrete picture.

trend_formats.name: The slow friend and the waiting friend
trend_formats.how: Borrow the situation of this month's 'go go go' videos (one person takes their time, the other stays polite), never the audio: it is someone else's sound and will be over before a film is made. The waiting is shown by one small repeated move on the beat, and then it flips.
trend_formats.episode_idea: Every Cat: Timo marches to the ground in a straight line while Luna stops to say hello to the ginger cat, he taps his yellow watch and says no more cats, and one cut later he sits on the kerb with the cat asleep on his lap, not daring to move, while Luna taps his watch.
trend_formats.shelf_life: The situation is evergreen. The named audio trend lasts weeks: do not use it.

trend_formats.name: The reaction close-up loop
trend_formats.how: A new 5 to 6 second edit cut from each film: one still face holding one feeling, framed so that it survives a square crop, with one line about the situation and never about the person. Posted between films as its own post, as a new edit and not a repost.
trend_formats.episode_idea: Faster Than Us (line: 'When the cat is faster than you'): Timo, with his cheek squashed flat on the suitcase, and Luna, with her cheeks puffed out, follow a fat cat with only their eyes as it strolls past them up the hill, and then they look at each other.
trend_formats.shelf_life: Evergreen. The named 'silent face' trend of this month lasts weeks; the reaction clip itself does not date.

trend_formats.name: The thing held back: what is in Big Yellow?
trend_formats.how: The standing question of the series, asked in the pinned comment and raised in the pilot by Timo's roast. Each time the suitcase opens it is a cut (closed, then already open) and it gives one thing, never the whole answer. Every film still stands alone. Give the first answer by the third or fourth film, so it never becomes a running joke that needs earlier films.
trend_formats.episode_idea: House: a sun-shower starts outside the ground and there is no roof anywhere, Luna pats Big Yellow, Timo says no, and one cut later both sit inside the open suitcase with the lid as a roof, dry, sharing her flatbread while the rain falls and the cat squeezes in between them.
trend_formats.shelf_life: Evergreen as a device. The question itself lasts months: it needs small answers along the way.

trend_formats.name: Result first
trend_formats.how: Show 0.8 seconds of the payoff picture first, then tell the story in order. Only as a second test version. It breaks the bible's rule of cause and effect in order and it is the kind of thing that made the client say he did not understand the plot, so it is published only if a silent-gate viewer still retells the story correctly. Otherwise the payoff frame becomes the cover.
trend_formats.episode_idea: No Scarf (opens with a flash of Timo in three scarves, a hat and a flag as a cape): Timo's rule for the day is no shopping, so he shakes his head at the smiling scarf seller, who only holds the scarf a little higher each time he looks back, and one cut later he walks away wearing all of it, prouder than anyone, with the seller waving.
trend_formats.shelf_life: Months. Measured as a top pattern this month in food, beauty and fitness; no figure was found for travel or football.

trend_formats.name: One fan ritual, one move together
trend_formats.how: The football-trip videos that travelled furthest in 2026 showed fans doing one simple thing together, not match action. The town gets its own small ritual (a clap), under three seconds, upper body only, never a dance and never a copy of a real team's ritual. This is the format the fan viewer asked for: something only people who go to matches recognise.
trend_formats.episode_idea: The Clap: outside the gate Luna joins the home fans' clap loudly and wrongly while Timo knows it but claps tiny and shy, a local fan their age offers to show her, she says no, she knows it, and one cut later he is teaching her clap by clap with big slow arms until all three clap over their heads together.
trend_formats.shelf_life: Months for the 2026 wave of fan-ritual videos; fan behaviour itself is evergreen. The named rituals of last summer will date, so none is copied.

posting_kit.caption:
One night. One suitcase. She calls it the small one. Plan or No Plan: which one are you?

Plan, No Plan: One Night. AI animation, written and designed by people.
posting_kit.comment_prompt: Pinned first comment from the account: 'What is in Big Yellow? She won't tell us either.' One comment, one line, never 'tag a friend'. Replies kept ready, each used once: to 'is this AI?': 'Yes, AI animation. The jokes, the designs and the music are ours.' To 'tourists' or 'half-and-half scarf': 'Half him, half her. We know.' To 'so what happened to the suitcase?': 'Big Yellow watched from the bag drop. The cat kept it company.' To 'what is Venuvoy?': 'The app that plans a football trip from one sentence. These two would never use it the same way.'
posting_kit.cover_text: No added text. The cover is the frame at about one second: Luna on the left, Big Yellow in the middle, Timo pointing on the right, with the baked line 'When your friend packs for one night' at the top. Every later film uses the same composition with its own big object in the middle, so the profile grid reads as a row of bright objects.
notes: AI label switched on at upload on TikTok, Reels and Shorts, for the pilot and for every cut-down. One line in the account bio says it too. Answer 'is this AI?' once and plainly; never delete or argue with 'AI slop' comments.
The caption quotes the first exchange only. The gate ending is never in the post text: it is the reason to watch to the end.

Account line, where the brand is explained so the film does not have to: 'Two best friends. Football trips abroad. Venuvoy is the app that plans the trip from one sentence. AI animation, made by people.' Add how to say the name to the profile, in the founder's own spelling: two viewers did not know how to say it. Claim 'made by people' only for what is true (writing, design, voices, music).
Title pattern for every post: 'Plan, No Plan: One Night'. No numbers, no 'Part 2'. Make a playlist called 'Plan, No Plan' on TikTok and on Shorts with the pilot.
The same master file, with our own music mixed in, goes to all three platforms on the same day. Never add a sound in the app on the main post. Upload a private test from the real account first.

Have three finished films before the pilot goes out and release them inside the first ten days. Cut-downs come in the second week as new edits: the cheek-squash loop, the cat's blown fur, Timo's look at the gate.
The same four tags in the same order on every post. No tournament, league or club tag, never 'soccer'. No slang, no 'bestie', no 'POV' unless the camera really is the third friend.

Before posting, the three gates of the bible, and one new one from this test. Silent gate: the muted cut with every text covered (the top line too) is shown to a viewer of 18 to 25 and to an adult with English as a second language; their one sentence must match ours. Sound gate: three people aged 18 to 25 hear it on a phone and answer 'advert, or somebody's video?'.

Test the top line on and off, and the result-first opening, with viewers before posting, not by posting two versions. If a viewer calls the top line advert-like, it comes off and Timo's line goes back to 'It's one night!'.
Never write 'try it' and never show a fall: a child could copy a ride down a hill. The art-toy world keeps it a cartoon.

Say plainly to the client: the story of the pilot is not a trend. What is current is the telling: the app-style line, the cut on the beat, a club beat instead of a jingle, the post text. And say what the test found: all four cold viewers understood it (9 out of 10) and all four still saw a brand film, not a person's post. This version removes the tells they named; it does not hide that a company made it.

Check on the day, in the app: TikTok's Creative Center for the wording and formats in use that week, and each platform's help pages for the music and AI-label rules. The research behind this plan read search summaries only and could not open the pages or the apps. None of it is legal advice.
